name: SpaceX rideshare (Transporter)
tooltip: Share a rocket with dozens of other satellites. The cheapest way to orbit, but you go where the main customer goes and when it goes. Priced at $350,000 for the first 50 kg, so even a 12 kg CubeSat pays for 50 kg.
source: price: https://newspaceeconomy.ca/2026/02/27/spacex-rideshare-pricing-as-of-february-2026-what-it-costs-whats-included-and-how-buyers-budget-a-mission/ ($350,000 for up to 50 kg, then $7,000 per extra kg, to sun-synchronous orbit; other orbits are quoted individually). Suggested game cost: 0.35 plus 0.007 per kg above 50 kg

name: Rocket Lab Electron (dedicated)
tooltip: A small rocket that launches your satellite alone, into the orbit and on the date you choose, at about 20 times the price of a rideshare slot.

name: Falcon 9 (dedicated)
tooltip: A medium rocket that can carry a lunar spacecraft such as LRO with a large margin.
source: list price $74M in 2026: https://spacenexus.us/guide/cost-to-launch (older sources show $67M to $69.75M)

name: Falcon Heavy
tooltip: The most powerful rocket here. More capacity than a 2,000 kg lunar mission needs, so it costs more but leaves room for heavier designs.
